newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says NATO chief to visit Moscow in January.
newsitem.headline: Russia says NATO chief to visit Moscow in January.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana will visit Moscow in late January to discuss an accord between the alliance and Russia, a foreign ministry spokesman said Monday.
The accord is designed to formalise relations between the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and its former Cold War enemy and ease tensions over NATO's plans to expand eastwards.
Reading from an official statement, the official said that Solana had telephoned Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov earlier on Monday to arrange the meeting.

"An agreement was reached that, in line with the proposal by NATO at the alliance's council in Brussels, the first meeting between Y. M. Primakov and J. Solana will take place in Moscow in the second half of January 1997," the spokesman said by telephone.
Russia has repeated its opposition to expansion, but said last week it was prepared to take up NATO's offer of talks on a new security partnership.
In doing so, it set aside a previous demand that NATO put enlargement on ice before the start of any negotiations.

Solana has said he hopes a deal could be on track -- or perhaps agreed -- by the time of NATO's Madrid summit on July 8-9 at which it is expected to invite some former communist countries to open accession talks.
